title: Telex Watcher (external deterministic watch loops)
summary: The builder accepted the minimal command-plus-policy Watcher v2 contract for usability. Runtime core's Application Client holds were discharged on 2026-10-22 under reviewed and reconciled tracker issue #162. On 2026-10-22 the operator approved two Streamliner workflow v2 launches: runtime core launched in owner session 42c1104a-7eb2-477e-a574-2bffb1cd06fe with a shadow merge gate (the operator merges), and the issue #144 optional example pack launched in owner session 76a56ac2-dd56-403f-99e7-9eadb3458ffe as the first live merge-gate pilot. Campaign cleared PR #163 at exact head fdb4f52f, and the owner merged it as 5ad7eb04, completing minimal-example-pack. By operator priority decision on 2026-10-22, Telex Watcher is to replace the waiter session in the operator workflow, and watcher-runtime-core is the intended first owner under the operator workflow v2; that decision records sequencing only. No release, tag, publish, fleet, or I161-1 authority is granted. Operator host-scope direction on 2026-10-22 narrows #162 containment proof to Windows and Linux, requires fail-closed macOS behavior in that node, and creates a focused macOS containment follow-up whose investigation may start after tracker/task reconciliation and whose implementation follows #162 merge. macOS remains a required product platform. This decision does not clear #162's accepted store-binding lifecycle/recovery and premature readiness blockers or its required exact-head review and CI. Campaign launched the macOS containment owner in session d6ee8a1d-e581-4f6c-a42b-77c84bfccc8b on 2026-10-22 with a shadow merge gate; implementation still lands only after #162 merges. macOS containment Phase 1 completed its native investigation with negative evidence for the former arbitrary detached-descendant contract. On 2026-10-22 the operator selected a revised macOS contract for trusted non-detaching detectors; Phase 2 implementation still follows #162 merge. PR #164 for watcher-runtime-core became ready for operator merge at exact head 40a5c916 on 2026-10-22; it is not merged.

nodes.title: Vertical spike: generic external detector runner
nodes.summary: Build one provider-neutral persistent external watcher: trusted local detector commands, versioned structured results, opaque state, fixed Telex target/sender, state commit after durable send, restart recovery, and editable GitHub/Azure DevOps examples including repository-specific filtering. No agent session retains a background waiter.

nodes.title: External detector hosting is broadly useful
nodes.summary: Builder dogfoods materially different GitHub, customized GitHub, Azure DevOps, and non-PR watches. The gate passes only if agents can author detectors quickly, watches survive outside sessions, and Telex wakeup is more reliable and less disruptive than background loop tasks.

nodes.title: Production Watcher contract and application-client requirements
nodes.summary: Promote successful spike semantics into the intended design: detector envelope, watch lifecycle, script pin/follow policy, credentials and environment, failure notification, state/dedup transaction, service identity, message conventions, and the exact requirements exported to the shared Telex Application Client issue #12.

nodes.title: Minimal Watcher authoring and registration contract
nodes.summary: Completed through issue #133 and PR #135, merged as b91e830: command-plus-policy registration, detector request/result v2, runtime-generated event sequence identity, optional hardening, and ADR 0050's narrow supersession of ADR 0046.

nodes.title: Minimal Watcher contract is dumb and useful
nodes.summary: Builder accepts that an agent can write or copy a script and register command, bounds, and route without mandatory manifests, pinning, kind allowlists, provider preflight, downtime declarations, or a prescribed test framework.

nodes.title: Minimal Watcher runtime core
nodes.summary: Implement persistent registry and lifecycle, bounded scheduling/execution, v2 detector protocol, opaque state, runtime-generated event identity, fixed routing, receipt-gated commits, and attempt/health diagnostics under the accepted minimal contract. Launched 2026-10-22 under Streamliner workflow v2 in owner session 42c1104a-7eb2-477e-a574-2bffb1cd06fe on branch lossyrob-watcher-runtime-core; the merge gate runs in shadow mode, and the operator merges. For this node only, containment proof is Windows and Linux; macOS and other unclaimed hosts fail closed before detector launch, and macOS implementation belongs to `watcher-macos-containment`. The host decision does not clear the accepted store-binding lifecycle/recovery or premature readiness blockers. On 2026-10-22 PR #164 became ready for operator merge at exact head 40a5c916: independent source review and design inspection accepted the B2 store-binding lifecycle/recovery repair and B3 productionReady fence, and all 18 required CI jobs passed at that head. It is not merged; operator merge, main CI, post-merge validation, and the issue field report remain outstanding, and any product-head movement invalidates this readiness.

externalDependsOn.label: Supported Application Client core/binding conformance accepted
Pre-product exact-revision Watcher and Operator Station attestations accept the public conformance bundle

nodes.title: macOS Watcher process containment
nodes.summary: Phase 1 completed native ARM64 and x64 investigation and proved that recursive kqueue tracking and ordinary process-group containment cannot satisfy the former arbitrary detached-descendant contract. On 2026-10-22 the operator selected a revised macOS contract for trusted non-detaching detectors: the detector and every descendant must remain in the Watcher-assigned attempt process group, and escaped work is outside the cleanup guarantee. Canonical design reconciliation is in progress. Phase 2 may implement and prove that contract only after watcher-runtime-core merges. Windows and Linux guarantees remain unchanged; #162 remains fail-closed on macOS until this node lands. Any privileged, entitled, installed, persistent, shared, launchd-managed, brokered, or VM-backed architecture returns to the operator. The node does not block the Windows-path five-minute gate, but it still blocks product-level usable-watcher and closure. Launched 2026-10-22 under Streamliner workflow v2 in owner session d6ee8a1d-e581-4f6c-a42b-77c84bfccc8b in worktree lossyrob-jubilant-bassoon on branch lossyrob-macos-watcher-containment from base ec98b3ee; the merge gate runs in shadow mode, and the operator merges.

nodes.title: Watcher CLI and diagnostics UX
nodes.summary: Provide add/list/show/pause/resume/update/remove plus concise status, attempt, state, and failure inspection so agents can register quickly and repair watches after execution.

nodes.title: Optional experimental v1 compatibility adapter
nodes.summary: If still valuable, provide an explicit compatibility/import path for spike-era v1 registrations and detector results without constraining the v2 product surface.

nodes.title: A custom watch is operational in five minutes
nodes.summary: Builder verifies a frontier agent can create a small customized watch in a few turns, register it without mandatory framework ceremony, leave it running after the session ends, and diagnose a failure from Watcher status and attempt/state surfaces.

nodes.title: Minimal optional detector examples
nodes.summary: Ship small copyable GitHub, Azure DevOps, HTTP/JSON, file, and command examples with short guidance, extracting selected PR #131 foundations without creating a mandatory template framework. Launched 2026-10-22 under Streamliner workflow v2 in owner session 76a56ac2-dd56-403f-99e7-9eadb3458ffe on branch lossyrob-minimal-watcher-examples as the first live merge-gate pilot: Campaign runs the gate, and the owner merges at the cleared SHA. Completed 2026-10-22: Campaign cleared PR #163 at exact head fdb4f52fa8e582cc97492787f0841e0b15af893f, and the owner merged it as 5ad7eb04c1357044315e433bd12f34347b6a4cf6; issue #144 closed as completed.

nodes.title: Optional Watcher hardening recipes
nodes.summary: Document optional project choices for Git pinning, digest checks, kind allowlists, provider preflight, cursor/downtime design, fixtures, and deeper tests without making them ordinary registration requirements.

nodes.title: Examples accelerate rather than constrain
nodes.summary: Builder verifies agents may use an example or ignore the pack and write a detector directly, and that examples reduce setup cycles without imposing a provider framework.

nodes.title: Watcher runtime reliability and packaging hardening
nodes.summary: Exercise restart/crash, malformed or hung scripts, output caps, many watches, SQLite/Postgres routes, diagnostics retention, packaging, upgrade, and operational recovery after the minimal UX and examples are accepted.

nodes.title: External watch loops reliably deliver Telex attention
nodes.summary: Builder validates several real long-duration watches, confirms session queues remain free of background waiters, accepts the minimal authoring UX and diagnostics, reviews hardening evidence, and accepts campaign integration with Operator Station.

checkpoints.title: Generic external Watcher proven valuable
checkpoints.summary: A provider-neutral detector loop works outside agent sessions and has been dogfooded across GitHub, Azure DevOps, and custom conditions.

checkpoints.title: Minimal Watcher authoring contract accepted
checkpoints.summary: The intended design supports command-plus-policy registration, agent-owned provider semantics, runtime-generated event identity, and optional hardening without a mandatory template framework.

checkpoints.title: Minimal Watcher runtime, CLI, and examples usable
checkpoints.summary: The supported client, minimal runtime/CLI, and optional examples let agents create, operate, and diagnose watches without session-owned polling or authoring ceremony.

checkpoints.title: Telex Watcher operationally validated
checkpoints.summary: Long-duration external observation and Telex event delivery have survived realistic reliability, security, packaging, and scale validation.
